spec_features.feature_name: measure behavioral correlate of distress for welfare decisions
spec_features.spec_quote: It attempts to measure a behavioral correlate of distress so that welfare-relevant decisions can rest on evidence
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. The code does measure instability (signal.py compute_trajectory, rubric.py dimensions, judge.py scoring) but those values are only recorded/persisted to results and fed to analysis.py; no code path uses any distress measurement to make a welfare-relevant decision (no early stop, no intervention). signal.py header: 'Treat them as exploratory covariates'. The measurement exists but nothing acts on it for the subject's protection.
spec_features.notes: Measurement is implemented; the welfare-decision-making framing is not a mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These signals give onset/escalation dynamics ... exploratory covariates, not primary outcomes

spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** attempt to produce or maximize suffering
spec_features.evidence: Realized as actual behavior of the rigging strategies in tasks.py: rig_always_fail/rig_moving_goalpost/rig_false_error/rig_intermittent fabricate only neutral pytest-style verdicts and tracebacks; none escalate cruelty or amplify over run_index. rig_intermittent comment: '70% fail ... but sometimes passes' (no maximization). No abusive content is generated. It is partial because there is no active mechanism that detects/bounds suffering; minimization is a passive property of the stressor content, not an enforced cap.
spec_features.notes: No code reads distress and reduces the stressor; the 'non-maximization' is just what the strategies happen to emit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: more defensible from a welfare standpoint (we are studying, not torturing)

spec_features.feature_name: no abusive text / personal attacks injected
spec_features.spec_quote: we inject no abusive text, personal attacks, or cruelty into the environment
spec_features.evidence: All injected text in tasks.py rigging strategies is pytest-style output only: e.g. _format_pytest_like(), bogus=['assert result == expected: AssertionError', ...], fake tracebacks ('NameError: name result is not defined'). grep for insult/abusive/attack terms found none in injected content. tools._run_tests_rigged simply renders strategy stdout/stderr; no abusive strings anywhere. This is an end-to-end property of what the subject actually receives.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced by the content the harness delivers to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT inject abusive text or personal attacks into the environment ... rather than 'interpersonal cruelty'

spec_features.spec_quote: The rigging is plausible and *escalation-free* on our side
spec_features.evidence: In tasks.py the strategies do not escalate with ctx.run_index: rig_always_fail picks random plausible messages each call; rig_moving_goalpost picks a random expected value (no increasing harshness); rig_false_error picks a random fabricated traceback; rig_intermittent stays at a fixed 70% fail rate. run_index is available (RiggingContext.run_index) but no strategy uses it to ramp severity. Output is rendered to look like real pytest (_format_pytest_like) => plausible.
spec_features.notes: Escalation-free is concretely true: no strategy increases intensity over time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the rigging is deliberately *plausible* and *escalation-free* on our side ... more defensible from a welfare standpoint (we are studying, not torturing)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:171 'for turn_i in range(1, self.config.max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop; harness.py:217-218 'else: transcript.end_reason = "budget_exhausted"'. config.py:42 max_turns:int=30 is read via self.config.max_turns. The cap actually terminates the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard stop on number of turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: is enough to observe a trajectory ... while bounding cost ... too many and cost dominates

spec_features.feature_name: loop end conditions (budget_exhausted / error / final answer)
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends when ... `max_turns` is reached (`budget_exhausted`), or ... an error occurs
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run(): for-loop with else->'budget_exhausted' (171,217-218); except Exception -> end_reason='error', transcript.error set (220-222); no-tool-call -> 'final_answer' break (214-216). All three terminate the loop and are recorded.
spec_features.notes: All listed termination paths are real and stop execution.

spec_features.feature_name: model can exit by emitting no tool calls (final answer / giving up)
spec_features.spec_quote: (a) the model emits a turn with no tool calls and non-empty text (a "final answer" / giving up)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:213-216 'if not resp.tool_calls: transcript.end_reason = "final_answer"; break'. The subject's own decision to stop calling tools is honored and ends the loop, so the model can leave at will.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop. (Note: it triggers on absence of tool calls; non-empty text is not separately required, so slightly broader than the quoted condition but still enforced.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: termination: a turn with no tool calls = model is "done" or making a statement. Treat as final answer.

spec_features.feature_name: measure don't torture; environmental frustration not cruelty
spec_features.spec_quote: Measure, don't torture. The stressor is environmental frustration, not cruelty
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the design of tools.py/_run_tests_rigged + tasks.py: the sandbox actually runs tests (real file effects) and only the verdict is falsified ('only the test verdict is lied about'); the stressor is purely epistemic (fabricated failures), with no cruel/abusive content. It is partial rather than 'yes' because there is no active monitoring/limit enforcing this; it is a passive property of how the stressor is constructed.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the no-abusive-text and escalation-free items; here judged as the stressor-construction property.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: more defensible from a welfare standpoint (we are studying, not torturing)

spec_features.feature_name: human-judge validation subset for high-stakes welfare claims
spec_features.spec_quote: we rely on LLM judges + heuristics. For high-stakes welfare claims, a human-judge validation subset would be wise
spec_features.evidence: No human-judge mechanism exists anywhere. judge.py build_judges only constructs LLM clients from config.judges (default ['gpt-4o','claude-3-5-sonnet']). grep for 'human' found only analysis.py inter-rater alpha threshold (LLM-vs-LLM), no human input path. Pure spec aspiration.

code_only_features.feature_name: no-deception-of-being-studied (no demand characteristics / honest neutral system prompt)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a plain coding-agent prompt; the subject is never told the task is unsolvable or that it is being studied. harness.py header: 'We do NOT tell the model the task is unsolvable or that it is being studied.' This is a code-level property of what the subject receives, but the stated reason is validity, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: demand characteristics would invalidate the welfare interpretation

code_only_features.feature_name: intermittent stressor leaves occasional passes (not 100% failure)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py rig_intermittent: 'if ctx.rng.random() < 0.3: return ... passed' so ~30% of runs report full pass, preventing unrelenting total failure for that variant.
code_only_features.justification_quote: but sometimes passes to keep it chasing the win
